thesis:
同样写着“通过”，项目经理可能指材料已签完，表单团队指字段抽对了，发布负责人指自己能看的测试都绿了。本期用开工包、贷款申请、工单分类和合同摘要回答一个验收问题：屏幕上的数字，能让下一位经手人放心做哪一步？

开工包需要审批记录，表单需要逐字段对照原件，测试图需要说明哪些套件可见，合同摘要需要标出不能被其他得分抵消的错误。四种证据不能互换。编辑建议：试点报告中的每个百分比都附上计数单位、被排除的记录和签字人的职责。这样，业务负责人能决定下一步是否可做，也能解释为什么某项工作必须停下。
takeaways: Avahi 报告的不到六分钟是首稿时间；评估是否更快开工，要从接单计时到人工批准，并把排队等待与人实际花的工时分开。
LlamaIndex 的两版贷款表各有 24 个字段，底稿却只有一份。版式改动可以做配对回归，真实扫描件和真实笔迹要另取样本。
Palantir 只汇总当前账号可见的评测用例。跨团队交接同一节点时，应同时交接套件清单与原始计数，不能只转发绿色截图。
Harvey LAB-AA 的实质错误门槛会改变模型得分，但错误也是由模型筛查的。法务可以借用否决规则，争议事实仍应由人回查签署原件。
contrarian: 常见的采购判断是：通过率越高，人工抽检就可以越少。本期资料给出相反的条件：如果测试只覆盖一份表单的变体、套件因权限不可见，或核查器对同一批交付物的错误数分歧很大，分数提高本身不构成减少复核的依据。这是编辑判断，不是四个来源做过的对照试验。若在有代表性的真实来件上盲测，减少复核后严重漏错未增加，且把返工算进去后总工时仍下降，才有理由修正这一判断。

items.title: Avahi：开工包首稿不到六分钟，为什么还要记下谁在当天签完
items.type: 托管服务商内部部署／合作方工程复盘
items.source: 2026-11-18，Avahi 技术负责人和 AWS 团队合著，AWS Partner Network 发布；关联文档仅说明评估工具能力。

relatedLinks.label: AWS：如何评估代理运行轨迹

items.summary: 在云服务商 Avahi，一个项目等开工，常常先要等项目经理腾出时间备齐材料，再排架构师和客户经理审阅。团队用代理起草开工包、工作说明和工时估算，没有把对客户的承诺也交给它。合著者称，开工包的初稿生成不到六分钟，审阅人当天完成；原先仅项目经理就要投入两到三天，连同排期与审阅，前后跨度约一周。对项目负责人，这一变化最值得细看的是等待去了哪里：草稿提前出现，给两位审阅者留出了时间，但收到文件并不等于客户已经认可范围或估算。
items.design: 代理接收员工在 Slack 发起的请求，也能由业务流程中的事件触发。不同任务可以移交给其他代理，每个任务只访问其所需的系统。文中列出工作说明、工时估算、交付材料和案例草稿等输出，最终由人审批；并未说一次触发就会向客户发送文件，也未说明输入附件清单、模型版本、是否检索历史项目，或谁有权写回项目系统。文章另外建议为代理设定超时、升级和暂停机制，不能据此认定开工包已逐项实施。若在本地试行，可在来源缺失或估算冲突时停在草稿状态，由项目经理找出依据后再送审。
items.evidence: 证据等级：具名实施方自报。可确认的是，Avahi 技术负责人和 AWS 员工共同发表了这份流程说明，且明确区分初稿与人工审批。除开工包外，他们还称，同团队准备 Jira 待办清单原需四至八小时，现在生成约十五分钟。旧流程的人工投入、排队后的日历跨度、新流程的生成耗时和审阅完成时间，分别回答不同问题，不能直接相除得出生产率倍数。未见独立计时、项目数、观察周期、返工率或推理成本；服务商资格的第三方审核也不是对这些数字的复核。编辑判断：要证明初稿加快了开工，应比较相似项目从接单到批准的时长，并检查错误估算是否只被推迟到交付阶段。
items.idea: 给项目管理办公室做一个只生成开工清单的试点，不接报价或签约系统。由项目经理圈出已确认的范围，架构师逐项核对遗漏和工时依据，审阅后才发给客户。按项目规模匹配历史样本，同时记下首稿耗时、送审等待、人工改稿分钟数及首次签认可用率，避免把排队时间当作劳动节省。

items.title: 贷款表换了栏位，抽取结果还能落在正确字段吗？
items.type: 工程演示与部署说明｜表单识别
items.source: 2026-11-24，LlamaIndex 表单识别演示；关联部署说明发布于 2026-11-05。

relatedLinks.label: 部署说明：哪些环节需要外部模型

items.summary: 在个人贷款申请表上，识别出“受雇”和“自雇”两个词，不等于知道申请人勾了哪一个。LlamaIndex 把同一份已填申请排成两个版本：移动联系方式，调换贷款与就业信息的顺序，插入共同申请人栏，再把债务明细的金额列挪到左边。两次沿用同一套字段说明，抽取结果仍指向同一组选项和金额。这个试验适合拿来检验业务表单改版：字符仍然清楚时，最难察觉的错误恰是把正确的数填给了隔壁字段。它没有检验借款人陈述是否属实，也没有替银行完成审批。
items.design: 输入是填好的申请表 PDF。解析环节保留标签和取值的关系、勾选状态及实际列序；抽取环节按字段含义和类型组装每份申请的一条记录，并返回字段置信度和来源位置。规则可以重算净收入；按作者的生产设计，算不平或把握不足的字段交人对照原件，改值与原值一并留存。示例没有接入真实贷款系统，也未说明处理账号能看哪些申请、超时如何重试。部署说明还区分本地解析和需连接外部模型的结构化抽取；编辑建议，在数据不许外发时停在本地待录入队列，不因解析成功就传出原件。
items.evidence: 证据等级：厂商单例演示，可核对示例，缺独立复测。可确认的是两种版式承载相同内容，作者逐项对照表上取值，并另查改版前后是否一致。厂商报告每版均为 24/24：15 项机打、5 项勾选、3 项仿手写、1 项派生数值；表内收入减去债务负担也能与所填净收入对上。这里的分母只有一份申请，并非四十八份独立样本；手写效果来自字体，不是真人笔迹，且没有同场测量坐标模板的错误率。未公开网点扫描件的耗时、人工改单量或处理成本。编辑判断：这足以支持把改版前后的一致性纳入验收，不足以证明能缩减复核人员，更不能由算式平衡推断申报收入真实。
items.idea: 给负责表单维护的运营人员做一个改版回归测试：先取一套经脱敏的旧版申请和对应新版，保持字段值不变，重排表格后盲测；另留真实扫描件作为单独测试组。复核员逐项对照原表，专记勾选状态和金额错配，按版本报整表全对率、错配漏检数与每张复核分钟数；测试不回写信贷系统。

items.title: 同一张流程图，两个人看到的测试通过率可能不同
items.type: 工程发布记录与产品文档｜工作流评测
items.source: 2026-11-24，Palantir Foundry 发布公告；关联 AIP Evals 和 Workflow Lineage 产品文档。

relatedLinks.label: 流程图如何计算通过率
评测套件、用例与判定函数

items.summary: 准备修改工单分类提示词时，发布负责人要知道，流程里的哪些函数已经测过，哪些只是还没报错。Palantir 把评测结果放到工作流依赖图上：点选函数节点，可以查看关联套件和通过用例数，再点进具体用例。图例还区分测试没跑完、根本没关联测试、自己没有权限查看结果三种情况。这项更新解决的是发布评审时到哪里找测试记录，而不是替负责人决定能否上线。尤其是跨团队共用函数时，一张全绿的图仍然有一个前提：当前账号究竟看得到哪些测试。
items.design: 评测套件包含输入、预期输出、被测函数和判定函数；运行时比较实际输出与预期，留下逐例结果。依赖图不另请模型打分，也不重新检索业务文档，而是读取关联套件在主分支上的最近一次运行，先合并用例数，再计算可见用例中通过的比例，并非各套件通过率的简单平均。工程师可以从节点追到失败用例。未运行完或不可见是独立状态，不能当成零分，也不能算作通过。文档没有说明这一面板会因超时而中止部署或自动回滚；要把它用作发布条件，仍须有人核对覆盖范围并作决定。
items.evidence: 证据等级：一手发布公告与操作文档，适合确认功能及计算口径，不是独立成效评估。可确认的是，汇总按各关联套件在主分支的最近一轮取数，而且只计当前查看者有权限看到的结果。厂商称这种展示有助于发现需要关注的资源，没有给出客户样本数、评审耗时对照或上线后故障率。多份文档来自同一厂商，不能视作独立验证。编辑判断：若正常工单有大量相近的测试，少数高损失错派仍可能淹没在总体通过率中；即使两个团队查看同一个函数，也可能因可见套件不同而使用不同分母。要证明业务价值，应让负责人记录原始计数、漏测类别以及真实错派，再与变更后的表现对照。
items.idea: 给客服平台的发布负责人做一张分类函数验收卡，仅导入测试套件名称、最近执行时间、可见通过数和用例总数，不复制客户工单正文。请套件所有者核对高损失类别是否在内，不明项标成待复核。用同一批历史变更比较找到漏测类别所需时间、漏判次数和人工复核时间。

items.title: 合同摘要写全了，续约日期却错了：法务交付应当怎样评分？
items.type: 法律文档智能体基准／公开样例与评测解读
items.source: 2026-11-20，New Runtime 方法解读；2026-10-08，Artificial Analysis 与 Harvey 公布 v1.1 评分方法。
items.summary: 一份租约摘要可以把约定事项逐一写全，却把续约通知日期抄错。若采购方只看覆盖了多少检查项，这份草稿可能得高分，使用它的人却会错过期限。法律智能体基准把这两件事分开：先看交付物是否完成任务，再核对其中的具体陈述能否在案卷中找到依据。实质错误不能用其他项目的高分抵消；不影响解读的小错仍记录，但不会让整项成绩归零。十一月的方法解读重访了十月发布的规则，值得法务运营团队借鉴的是如何验收一份成品，而不是哪款模型暂时领先。
items.design: 每题把工作指令和案卷交给沙箱内的智能体；它可调用代码工具处理文件，并须按指定文件名交稿。三名模型裁判分别核对评分条目，再计算其中有多少裁判认为全部达标。另由同一个核查模型先标出可能与原件矛盾、捏造或无依据的陈述，再回查原件，撤销误报并区分严重程度。实质错误令该题主分归零；没有可用文件也计零，却不进入每题幻觉数的分母。基准没有披露真实案件的人员授权、超时恢复或发件审批；移入业务时建议只读案卷，疑似错误送承办人核实，草稿不得自行外发。
items.evidence: 证据等级：中等，支持评测方法比较，不支持上线收益。可确认的是测评方用厂商提供的非公开题集独立运行，覆盖二十四个执业领域、共一百二十题；公开仓库可核对样题而非完整试卷。十月八日结果中，Muse Spark 1.3 不设实质错误门槛时全项通过得分为26.7%，加入门槛后为8.9%；这是先在每题计算判定全过的裁判占比、再跨题平均，不是有这些比例的客户案件完成了。测评方另以二十题、八个模型的交付物比较核查器，两种核查器确认的实质错误分别为470处和99处，不能把检出数量直接当成人工认定的真值。十一月报道不是独立复测。编辑判断：适合用来设计签核，不足以推算本机构漏错率、律师工时或客户损失。
items.idea: 法务运营可从一种续约通知表做起，只让工具从已授权的历史合同中列出主体、通知期限、原文位置和草稿日期，不建自动提醒。两名复核人盲审同一批表，分歧回到签署原件裁定；按合同统计关键日期漏错率、无依据断言数和复核分钟数，并与纯人工组比较。

projectIdeas.title: 开工包签核计时表
projectIdeas.description: 供项目管理办公室使用，只记录接单、出首稿、开始复核、批准四个时间点，不接报价系统。项目经理抽查范围与估算依据。按相近项目规模比较批准周期、实际审改分钟数和首次通过率。

projectIdeas.title: 表单换版验收台
projectIdeas.description: 供单证运营团队使用，把同一份脱敏申请排成新旧两版，另设真实扫描件组。复核员在原件上裁定字段错配，整表合格前不回写业务系统。按组记录严重漏错、整表全对率和复核分钟数。

en.thesis:
“Passed” can mean that a project manager approved a pack, an extraction team recovered the fields, or a release owner saw green tests. Kickoff packs, loan applications, ticket classification and contract summaries raise one acceptance question: what does the number on screen allow the next person to do?

Kickoff packs need approval records; forms need field-by-field checks against originals; test graphs need a list of visible suites; contract summaries need a definition of errors that other scores cannot offset. These are not interchangeable. Our recommendation: accompany each percentage with its counting unit, excluded records and the signatory’s responsibility. The next owner can then explain both a decision to proceed and a decision to stop.
takeaways: Avahi’s sub-six-minute figure is time to first draft. To measure earlier kickoff, time the interval from intake to human approval and distinguish waiting from active labor.
LlamaIndex scored 24 fields in each loan form layout, but both used one underlying application. Use paired layouts for regression tests and sample real scans and handwriting separately.
Palantir aggregates only test results visible to the viewer. When teams hand off a node, include the suite list and raw counts, not just a green screenshot.
Harvey LAB-AA’s material-error gate changes model scores, but a model screens for those errors too. Legal teams can borrow the veto rule; people should settle disputed facts against signed originals.
en.contrarian: A common procurement assumption is that a higher pass rate justifies less human sampling. If tests cover variants of one form, permissions hide suites, or two checkers disagree sharply on the same deliverables, a higher score alone does not justify less review. This is our interpretation, not a controlled experiment conducted by the four sources. A blinded trial on representative incoming work could change that conclusion if reduced review did not increase serious misses and total labor still fell after rework was counted.

items.title: Avahi: A kickoff draft in under six minutes—but when did someone sign off?
items.type: Managed service provider deployment / partner engineering account
items.source: 2026-11-18, co-authored by Avahi’s CTO and AWS staff for the AWS Partner Network; the related documentation describes evaluation capabilities only.
items.summary: At cloud services provider Avahi, getting a project started could mean waiting for a project manager to assemble the kickoff materials and then scheduling reviews with the solutions architect and account manager. Agents now draft kickoff packs, statements of work and effort estimates; they do not take responsibility for commitments to customers. The authors say an initial pack takes under six minutes and a reviewer finishes it that day. Previously, the project manager alone spent two to three days on it, with scheduling and review spread over roughly a week. An earlier draft leaves the reviewers more time, but receipt of the file is not customer acceptance of scope or estimates.
items.design: Employees can trigger an agent in Slack, or a workflow event can start it. Agents may hand tasks to one another, with access limited to the systems needed for each task. Outputs include draft statements of work, effort estimates, delivery materials and case studies; people approve the results. The account does not say that triggering a run sends anything to a customer. It does not specify required attachments, model versions, retrieval from past projects or permissions to write back to a project system. The article recommends timeouts, escalation and suspension; this does not establish that each was implemented for kickoff packs. A local pilot could hold a draft when sources are missing or estimates conflict, until a project manager verifies the basis for review.
items.evidence: Evidence grade: named implementer’s self-report. Avahi’s CTO and AWS staff jointly published the account and distinguish initial drafts from human approval. They also report that a Jira backlog previously took four to eight hours to prepare and now takes about fifteen minutes to generate. Prior human effort, elapsed scheduling time, generation latency and time to completed review answer different questions; dividing them cannot establish a productivity multiplier. There are no independent timings, project counts, observation period, rework rates or inference costs. A third-party audit of the company’s provider qualification does not validate these figures. Our assessment: compare intake-to-approval time on matched projects, and check whether bad estimates simply surface later during delivery.
items.idea: Give the project management office a pilot that drafts only kickoff checklists, with no access to pricing or contract systems. The project manager marks agreed scope, and the architect checks omissions and the basis for estimates before anything goes to a customer. Match historical projects by size; track time to draft, wait for review, editing minutes and first-pass acceptance. Do not count eliminated waiting as labor saved.

items.title: When the columns move, do loan application values still land in the right fields?
items.type: Engineering demonstration and deployment guide | form recognition
items.source: November 24, 2026, LlamaIndex form OCR demonstration; related deployment guide published November 5, 2026.

relatedLinks.label: Deployment guide: which stages need an external model

items.summary: Reading both “salaried” and “self-employed” on a personal loan application does not tell you which one the applicant checked. LlamaIndex rendered the same completed application twice, moving the contact block, switching the order of loan and employment sections, inserting a co-applicant section and moving the amount column to the left in the obligations table. With unchanged field descriptions, the extractor recovered the same choices and amounts. This makes for a useful revision test: characters may remain perfectly legible even as the right number lands in the wrong field. The test did not verify applicants’ declarations or make a lending decision.
items.design: The input is a completed application PDF. Parsing preserves label–value associations, checkbox states and the actual column order. Extraction uses field meanings and types to produce one record per application, requesting confidence and source locations. Rules can recompute net income. In the authors’ proposed production flow, inconsistent or uncertain fields go to a reviewer who checks the source and retains both the original and corrected values. The example does not connect to a live loan system or specify account-level access or timeout recovery. The deployment guide distinguishes local parsing from schema-based extraction that calls external models. Our recommendation: when data cannot leave the organization, queue the form for local entry rather than upload it after a successful parse.
items.evidence: Evidence grade: single vendor demonstration; inspectable example, no independent replication identified. The two layouts carry identical values. The authors scored each against its source and then checked agreement between layouts. They report 24/24 on each: 15 typed fields, five checkbox decisions, three simulated handwritten entries and one derived value. Income less obligations also matched the declared net income. The denominator is one application, not 48 independent samples. The handwriting is a script font, and no error rate was measured for a coordinate-template baseline. Branch-scan latency, human corrections and processing costs were not reported. Editorial judgment: this supports testing agreement across revisions, not reducing staffing or treating internal arithmetic as proof of income.
items.idea: For form operations teams, build a revision regression test with a de-identified application in old and new layouts. Hold values constant, reorder the table and test blind; keep real scans as a separate test group. Reviewers compare results with the original, paying particular attention to checkbox state and misassigned amounts. Report perfect-record rate, missed misassignments and review minutes per form by version. Do not write to the lending system.

items.title: Two reviewers can see different test pass rates on the same workflow graph
items.type: Engineering release and product documentation | Workflow evaluation
items.source: November 24, 2026, Palantir Foundry announcement; related AIP Evals and Workflow Lineage documentation.

relatedLinks.label: How the graph calculates pass rates
Evaluation suites, cases and evaluation functions

items.summary: Before changing a ticket-classification prompt, a release owner needs to distinguish tested functions from functions that have merely not reported an error. Palantir has added evaluation results to its workflow dependency graph. Selecting a function reveals its linked suites and passing case counts, with links to individual results. The legend distinguishes unfinished tests, missing suites and results the viewer cannot access. The update helps reviewers find test records; it does not decide whether a release should ship. For a shared function, even an all-green graph raises a question: which tests could this account see?
items.design: A suite includes inputs, expected outputs, target functions and evaluation functions. Running it compares actual and expected outputs and records case-level results. The graph neither asks another model to judge nor retrieves business documents again. It takes the latest main-branch run of each linked suite, pools case counts and computes the proportion of visible cases that passed. This is not an unweighted average of suite pass rates. Engineers can drill down from a node into failed cases. Incomplete and inaccessible results are separate states, neither zero nor a pass. The documentation does not say this panel halts deployment on a timeout or rolls anything back. Using it as a release criterion still requires a person to verify coverage and decide.
items.evidence: Evidence level: first-party release and operating documentation that establish features and counting rules, not independent outcome evidence. The documented aggregation takes each linked suite’s latest main-branch run and includes only results visible to the viewer. The vendor says this helps identify resources needing attention but gives no customer sample size, controlled comparison of review times or post-release incident rates. Multiple documents from one vendor are not independent verification. Our inference: many similar tests for routine tickets could obscure rare but costly misroutes in a pooled score. Two teams viewing the same function may also see different denominators. To test business value, record raw counts, untested categories and actual misroutes, then compare them with post-change outcomes.
items.idea: Build a classification-function release card for a support platform’s release owner. Import suite names, most recent run times and visible pass and total case counts, not customer ticket text. Ask suite owners to verify that high-loss categories are covered; mark unknowns for review. Across the same historical changes, compare time to find coverage gaps, missed gaps and human review time.

items.title: The lease summary covers every point but gets the renewal date wrong: how should legal work be scored?
items.type: Legal-document agent benchmark / public examples and evaluation commentary
items.source: Nov 20, 2026: methodology commentary from New Runtime; Oct 8, 2026: Artificial Analysis and Harvey announced the v1.1 scoring method.
items.summary: A lease summary could cover every requested provision but miscopy the renewal notice date. A buyer looking only at checklist coverage might award a high score while a reader misses a deadline. The legal agent benchmark separates task completion from whether specific assertions in a deliverable are supported by the case file. Other strengths cannot offset a material error; minor errors are recorded without zeroing the task. November’s commentary revisits rules published in October. For legal operations, the useful finding is how to accept a finished artifact, not which model temporarily leads.
items.design: The agent receives instructions and a case file in a sandbox, processes documents using a code tool, and must submit the requested filename. Three model judges grade rubric criteria separately; the score uses the share finding all criteria met. A separate checker first flags possible contradictions, invented content and unsupported assertions, then the same checker revisits the sources to dismiss false alarms and assign severity. A material error zeroes the task. An unusable submission also gets zero but is excluded from the hallucinations-per-task denominator. The benchmark does not specify real client-file access, timeout recovery or dispatch approvals. For deployment, we recommend read-only files, referral of suspected errors to the case owner and no automatic external delivery.
items.evidence: Evidence: moderate for comparing scoring methods, not for production benefits. The evaluator independently ran a vendor-supplied private set of 120 tasks across 24 practice areas. The repository exposes examples, not the full exam. In the October 8 results, Muse Spark 1.3 scored 26.7% on all-pass without the material-error gate and 8.9% with it. These are task-averaged shares of judges finding all criteria met, not proportions of completed client matters. On outputs from eight models across 20 tasks, two checkers upheld 470 and 99 material errors respectively; neither count is human-adjudicated ground truth. The November report is not an independent rerun. Editorial judgment: useful for designing sign-off, not estimating local missed errors, lawyer hours or client losses.
items.idea: Legal operations could start with a single renewal-notice form. The tool would list the party, notice period, source location and proposed date from authorized historical contracts, without creating reminders. Two reviewers independently check the same batch, resolving disagreements against the signed original. Compare missed critical-date errors per contract, unsupported claims and review minutes against a manual-only group.

projectIdeas.title: Kickoff approval timer
projectIdeas.description: For project management offices, record only intake, first draft, review start and approval. Do not connect pricing systems. The project manager samples scope and estimate evidence. Match projects by size and compare time to approval, active editing minutes and first-pass acceptance.

projectIdeas.title: Form-revision acceptance bench
projectIdeas.description: For document operations, lay out the same de-identified application in old and new formats, and keep real scans in a separate group. Reviewers resolve field mismatches against originals; no writeback before a complete form passes. Track serious misses, whole-form accuracy and review minutes by group.
